title: Record the state-store decision: drop the live state.json write-through cache
description: Create docs/architecture/state-store.md as the SPEC Requirement 8 decision doc. It records: (a) .datum/state.json as a LIVE write-through cache is dropped — save_state()/update_state() will stop writing it; (b) .datum/runs/<run_id>/state.json survives unchanged as the point-in-time archival export (rollback.py / archive.py / closeout archive); (c) datum/state.py's load_state/save_state/update_state are the canonical in-process accessor with unchanged signatures, and load_state() returning {} means 'no state' (never raises); (d) the two permanent documented exceptions — datum/memory/corpus_sql.py (read-only sqlite ATTACH of state.db, needs SQL-queryable access) and datum-tui/data.py (must not import the datum package); (e) migrate.py becomes a one-shot legacy state.json importer; (f) the incremental per-module migration order used by this epic. Docs-only, no code.
acceptance_criteria: docs/architecture/state-store.md exists and explicitly states option (a) of SPEC Requirement 8: the .datum/state.json live write-through cache is dropped, save_state()/update_state() no longer write it
The doc states that .datum/runs/<run_id>/state.json archival snapshots are unaffected and remain the supported export format

The doc names datum/state.py load_state/save_state/update_state as the canonical accessor with unchanged signatures, and states that load_state() returning {} means 'no state written yet' and must never raise

The doc lists exactly two permanent documented exceptions — datum/memory/corpus_sql.py (SQL-queryable ATTACH of state.db) and datum-tui/data.py (no datum-package import) — with the structural reason for each
The doc records migrate.py's chosen fate: retargeted as a one-shot legacy state.json importer (SPEC Requirement 3 option b)
red_note: Structural/docs-only — no test stage. This lane exists because SPEC Requirement 8 and Requirement 3 both declare an open choice that every later lane has to cite; writing it first stops each migration lane from re-deciding it. Scope note for the reviewer: the epic's QUESTIONS.md answers for Q5 (a SCHEMA_VERSION constant in state.py), Q6 (a 5s sqlite busy_timeout) and Q7 ('a missing db must raise a named error, never return {}') are deliberately NOT decomposed into tasks — the SPEC takes affirmative positions against all three (Out of Scope bars schema-versioning and new locking primitives; '{} means no state' is asserted in the Failure Modes table, in Requirement 9's AC, and implied by Requirement 1's no-breaking-signature-change AC). Making load_state() raise would invalidate the AC task-010 is built on. State that omission in this doc so it is visible rather than discovered at review.

After this lane, `datum status`-style rendering reads .datum/state.db instead of .datum/state.json — one thing a real caller could not do before.
acceptance_criteria: datum/status_render.py contains no `STATE_FILE = Path(".datum/state.json")` and no `def load_state`

datum/status_render.py's render path obtains state via `from datum.state import load_state` (or an equivalent direct call into datum.state) and renders the same output for the same state dict as before migration
datum/cli.py no longer imports load_state from datum.status_render; the status command resolves state via datum.state.load_state

render() applied to the dict returned by datum.state.load_state() for a fixture state containing a `phases` map produces the same rendered text as the pre-migration JSON-backed path produced for the identical dict

title: migrate.py becomes a one-shot legacy state.json importer with renamed entry points
description: SPEC Requirement 3, resolved to option (b) by task-001's decision doc: migrate.py keeps reading .datum/state.json, but solely as a one-shot legacy import into state.db, and says so in a comment at the top of the file. Because SPEC Requirement 1's AC forbids `def load_state`/`def save_state` outside datum/state.py, migrate.py's helpers are renamed (e.g. load_legacy_state / commit_migrated_state, the latter delegating to datum.state.save_state), which forces the matching update at its only caller, datum/cli.py:849.

Add a test that a repo with neither state.json nor .wfc/ produces the 'Nothing to do' path with exit 0. FILE-SHARING NOTE: datum/cli.py is owned by task-002 (which removes the status_render load_state import at cli.py:11); this lane depends_on task-002 and edits a different region (the migrate command's import block at cli.py:849). title: Make corpus_sql and datum-tui the two documented exceptions, both off the live state.json
description: SPEC Requirements 5 and 7. corpus_sql.py keeps its read-only ATTACH of .datum/state.db (it needs SQL-queryable access, not a Python dict) with an explanatory comment above the block, and drops the DuckDB view built over the raw .datum/state.json file (lines 431-434) since that file is about to stop existing — analytics queries must return the same column names with state.json absent. datum-tui/data.py keeps its own load_state() and its no-datum-import property, but its backing store swaps from the JSON file to a stdlib sqlite3 read of .datum/state.db, with a comment naming this epic and the exemption reason.

red_note: Two new pytest files; tests/test_corpus_sql.py is existing coverage that has no state.json reference and is NOT owned by this lane — if it needs editing, stop and report. tests/test_corpus_sql_state_json_absent.py: with .datum/state.json deleted and only state.db present, run the analytics query and assert the exact set of result column names matches the documented pre-migration set — RED fails today because the missing-file view breaks or drops columns. tests/test_datum_tui_data_state.py: save state via datum.state.save_state in the fixture, then call datum-tui data.load_state() and assert it returns those values, plus a case asserting {} on a missing db; also assert the module source contains no `import datum` / `from datum`. SPEC-DRIFT PRE-EMPTION for the reviewer: Requirement 7 says datum-tui 'retains its own load_state() implementation' — it does, and it still imports no datum package; only the backing store swaps to state.db, because task-001's Requirement 8 decision removes the JSON file it currently reads.

title: Closeout archive snapshots live state from state.db instead of copying state.json
description: datum/closeout/archive.py currently shutil.copy2's the live .datum/state.json into .datum/runs/<run_id>/state.json and then unlinks it — an undisclosed live-cache consumer that breaks silently the moment task-012 stops writing that file. It is repointed to serialise datum.state.load_state() into the run's state.json snapshot, keeping the archival export byte-compatible for downstream consumers, and to stop reporting archived_to for a snapshot it never wrote.
acceptance_criteria: datum/closeout/archive.py writes `.datum/runs/<run_id>/state.json` from `json.dumps(datum.state.load_state(), indent=2)` rather than shutil.copy2 of `.datum/state.json`
The archived `.datum/runs/<run_id>/state.json` contains exactly the dict returned by datum.state.load_state() at archive time
archive.py still copies `.datum/state.db` to `.datum/runs/<run_id>/state.db` and still unlinks the live `.datum/state.db` after a successful archive

When load_state() returns {} (no state ever written), archive.py does not report an archived_to path pointing at a file it did not create — it either omits archived_to or reports the run dir with an explicit empty-state marker
The `.archive.done` marker short-circuit is unchanged: a second invocation for the same run_id prints {"ok": true, "skipped": true} and performs no writes
red_note: This lane owns two EXISTING test files that assert the current copy-from-state.json behaviour: tests/test_closeout_scripts.py (the archive block around lines 361-500, including the documented archived_to-points-at-a-nonexistent-file bug) and tests/test_closeout_cli.py (lines 68-72, which write .datum/state.json and assert it is moved to .datum/runs/r1/state.json). RED: rewrite those fixtures to seed state via datum.state.save_state and never create .datum/state.json, then assert .datum/runs/<run_id>/state.json contains the seeded dict — fails today because archive.py finds no state.json to copy. This lane must land before task-012 drops the write-through, otherwise closeout archiving silently produces empty runs.

title: Closeout collectors emit an explicit no_state_available sentinel instead of exiting
description: SPEC Requirement 9 — the FU-4 bug that motivated the epic: 'no telemetry available' was indistinguishable from 'zero work happened'. collect_tasks.py currently sys.exit(1)s (line 125) before writing anything when it finds no lane-state markers and no state; collect_token_metrics.py similarly bails with a reason string. Both instead write their raw file with an explicit named sentinel, and collate.py surfaces that sentinel in closeout-data.json rather than a null/zero, while also dropping its now-dead fallback to the live `.datum/state.json` (line 57).
acceptance_criteria: When datum.state.load_state() returns {} and no lane-state markers exist, collect_tasks.py writes `.datum/runs/<run_id>/closeout-raw/tasks.json` containing `{"status": "no_state_available"}` (plus its usual envelope fields) and exits 0 instead of sys.exit(1)
collect_tasks.py still exits 0 with real task metrics, and no sentinel, when lane-state markers do exist — the happy path is unchanged

collect_token_metrics.py writes its raw file with the same `{"status": "no_state_available"}` sentinel when no state.db is present at either `.datum/runs/<run_id>/state.db` or `.datum/state.db`, instead of only recording a free-text reason
collate.py's rendered `closeout-data.json` shows a non-null, non-zero value for `tasks` in the no-state case — specifically the propagated `"no_state_available"` sentinel, not None and not 0
collate.py no longer falls back to the live `.datum/state.json` when `.datum/runs/<run_id>/state.json` is absent; `grep -n '\.datum/state\.json' datum/closeout/collate.py` returns zero matches
red_note: All three files ship together because the sentinel value is one contract spanning producer and collator — testing collate independently cannot prove the sentinel survives the hop. This lane owns two EXISTING test files: tests/test_closeout_collectors.py (the collect_tasks/collect_token_metrics blocks, including the zero-lanes case around line 882) and tests/test_closeout_collate.py. RED: run collect_tasks in a repo with no lane-state markers and no state.db and assert closeout-raw/tasks.json exists and parses to a dict whose 'status' == 'no_state_available' — today the process exits 1 and the file is never written. Then a second test running the collectors and collate end-to-end asserting closeout-data.json['tasks'] carries the sentinel (assert it is not None and not 0 explicitly — that pair is the actual FU-4 regression). GUARD: tests/test_closeout_cli.py is owned by task-009; its collect_tasks test only exercises the arg-forwarding happy path, so it should not need edits — if it does, stop and report rather than editing it.
